key_insight: In wall-bounded turbulence, coherent Q structures are not automatically causally important: only about half are more influential than the same volume of incoherent turbulence, and their significance depends on local flow context.
engineering_relevance: This cautions flow-control and reduced-order models against treating all Q events as equally actionable targets, since only specific structure-environment combinations appear causally amplified.
method: Comparison of causal significance against equivalent incoherent volume
evidence_signal: The study evaluates causal significance across identified structures in wall-bounded turbulence and finds that only about half exceed an equivalent incoherent flow volume.
watch_item: Causal ranking is environment-dependent, so using quadrant labels alone as a homogeneous model class can misidentify which structures matter dynamically.
paper_title: Coherence does not always imply causality in wall-bounded turbulence
